This is Peter Lynch’s favorite metric and I like it too because it ties valuation to growth. I prefer using a 2026 to 2028 window so the multiple adjusts for how fast the business is actually compounding.  

For example, $SOFI may trade at ~26x forward earnings but earnings are expected to grow from $0.60 in 2026 to $1.05 in 2028 implying a ~30% earnings CAGR and a PEG of ~0.9x.

$SOFI took 11 years to reach its first 4M members and added nearly another 4M in the past year alone.

Thats why the top 10 bank thesis still feels early since SoFi holds less than 15% of the deposit base of today's number 10 U.S. bank while building a one-stop financial platform with 30%+ member growth.

The kicker is LPB (Loan Platform Business) which is the asset-light layer where SoFi earns a ~4.6% take rate on third-party originations with zero balance-sheet usage and zero credit risk.  

That creates a high margin, fee based lending revenue stream running at ~$12B annualized origination pace while SoFi still trades around 15x 2028 earnings.

Wild to see $AMD now trading at nearly 3x $NVDA forward earnings multiple with Nvidia at ~20x despite 90% AI GPU share, 75% gross margins and a path to $1T in cumulative Blackwell and Rubin revenue through 2027.

The market is paying AMD for rate of change after landing $META, $ORCL and OpenAI gigawatt commitments but the real decoupling came from the CPU bottleneck trade.

GPU deals re-rated AMD but the CPU trade is what helped it decouple from Nvidia as EPYC gains pricing power into tighter supply and hyperscalers “gobbling CPUs” for agentic workloads.
This is less a knock on $AMD and more a reflection of how cheap $NVDA looks to me here.
